description: Saves a motion-graphics look of the person's own, made from a reference they shared (screenshots or frames of a video they like, a poster, a website) or described in their words, so it is offered first in the looks picker for this and every later video. Write it from what you see, in the same fields as the looks tool's: the reference's style grammar only (palette with hex codes, type, layout, motion, pacing, texture), never its logos, characters, mascots, words, brand or creator. Title it for what it looks like ("Paper Cutout", "Neon Ledger"), never after a brand or person. Saving again under the same title replaces that look. Free. Returns its id for start_video's `look`.

best_for.description: The kinds of videos it suits, e.g. "money explainers, product walkthroughs"

description.description: One line, like the looks tool's

layout.description: How a frame is laid out: grid, margins, where the words and pictures sit

motion.description: How things move: entrances, exits, eases and how one scene hands over to the next

pacing.description: How fast it cuts and how long each idea holds on screen

palette.description: Ground, ink, accents, each with its hex code and what it is used for

reference.description: What they asked for, kept for their later videos in this look: their own words on the style as they wrote them, and the link if they gave one

scenes.description: When it was made from a video: its scene map, one line per scene (from–to seconds, what it is, what moves and how it hands over, how much is written on screen)

source.description: What it was made from in a few words, e.g. "4 screenshots of a finance explainer" (no links, no names)

texture.description: Surface and finish: grain, paper, gloss, shadows, outlines

title.description: What it looks like, 1 to 3 words; never a brand, creator or show name

type.description: Fonts (Google Fonts) and how they are set

name: save_look
title: Save their own look
